aggressive_definition: Higher-grade incident prostate cancer, defined as Gleason grade group >6 or ISUP grade groups 3+4+5.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: The associations between the adherence to the three dietary patterns and PCa risk (global, for Gleason grade groups 6 and >6, and for International Society of Urological Pathology [ISUP] grade 1 + 2 and ISUP grade 3 + 4 + 5) was explored with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models stratified by centre and age.
study_design: Prospective EPIC-Spain cohort analyzed with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The Spanish cohort of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition study provided dietary and epidemiological information from 15 296 men recruited during the period 1992-1996.
reason: The prospective cohort analyzed both global incident prostate cancer and explicitly higher-grade incident endpoints defined by Gleason and ISUP grade groups.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: While no effect on PCa risk was detected for the Prudent and Mediterranean dietary patterns, a suggestion of a detrimental effect of the Western dietary pattern was found (hazard ratio [HR]<sub>Q4vsQ1</sub> 1.29 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.96;1.72]).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported HR 1.29 is for overall PCa risk, not either of the higher-grade endpoints.

additional_estimates.comparison: Western dietary-pattern adherence, quartile 4 versus quartile 1
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: This effect was only observed for Gleason grade group >6 (HR<sub>Q3vsQ1</sub> 1.61 [95% CI 1.00; 2.59] and HR<sub>Q4vsQ1</sub> 1.60 [95% CI 0.96; 2.67])
